neighbours.label: ' their' opening an absolute clause after a comma that describes a dispersed group ('had emptied, their people moving away')
fire: After the war the mining towns slowly died, their families drifting south for work.
By 1850 the old clans had broken apart, their members settling across three states.
The fishing ports declined in the seventies, their young people leaving for the capital.
Within a decade the farms had been abandoned, their owners heading for the coast.
The monasteries were closed by the king, their monks scattering across Europe.
When the factory shut, the workers' estates emptied, their residents moving to new suburbs.
The mountain villages shrank each winter, their shepherds wandering down to the plains.
The guilds collapsed after the reforms, their craftsmen dispersing to other towns.
quiet: After the war the mining towns slowly died as families drifted south for work.
By 1850 the old clans had broken apart and settled across three states.
The fishing ports declined in the seventies when the herring disappeared.
Within a decade the farms had been abandoned and the fields had gone wild.
The monasteries were closed by the king and sold to local landowners.
When the factory shut, the workers' estates emptied within a few years.
The mountain villages shrank each winter as the roads became blocked.
The guilds collapsed after the reforms that opened the trades to all.
